members.name: Daniel Revach
members.bio: Nothing beats the pleasure of seeing this college magazine thrive on for its second year. During this “gap year” of mine, I’ve had the joy of editing content and helping the Reuby’s talented and passionate team navigate the intricate journey of putting together an issue shaped by the brilliant and diverse minds of Reuben College. And as with any proper journey, this one was coloured by new friendships, exciting challenges faced together, and growth. Till next time.

members.name: Jayroop Ramesh
members.bio: Practical vocations are worthwhile pursuits, whereas creative endeavors are essential to life, is a paraphrased quote from Dead Poets Society and one which I wholly believe in. As we at Reuben strive to bring AI supremacy (and possible apocalypse) to the domains of climate change, genomics, and healthcare through our day jobs, I feel that it’s essential to emphasize our collective humanity through the Reuby. I’m extremely elated to have worked with such an enthusiastic and encouraging editorial team, and I hope to continue our shared experiences together!

members.name: Prenika Anand
members.bio: Every time I was asked why I chose Reuben as my preferred college, I always emphasized how the values on which Reuben College was created are very much a reflection of my own. Working with the Reuby editorial team was an opportunity to honour the humane experience I had at Reuben. I hope the 'Humans of Reuben' section continues to celebrate stories of people who work tirelessly behind the scenes to make every student feel belonged.

members.name: Eliza Rayner
members.bio: I wanted to get involved with the Reuby because it seemed like a lovely way to contribute to our growing college community. I've been responsible for the graphic design of this issue - I wanted to be an artist before I ever thought of studying science, so I enjoy any opportunity to take on a creative project! It's been a joy to work with such a friendly, talented, and motivated team of people to make this issue possible, and I'm excited for the future of the Reuby as a shared creative outlet for the Reuben community.

members.name: Charlotte Lenhard
members.bio: I wanted to get involved with the Reuby because I think it’s wonderful to share more creativity, art, writing, and other beautiful things with each other. I did a one-year master’s in environmental governance this year and have never been more sure that we need more creativity - in and beyond university. I contributed to the Reuby team with some organisational support. Throughout the process, I have enjoyed being part of how the Reuby created space for new encounters.

members.name: Puyu Wang
members.bio: I am a DPhil student at the University of Oxford's e-Research Centre, where I work on Semantic Web technologies and their applications across various sectors. Prior to my current research, I studied musicology in Shanghai. In my spare time, I enjoy playing the piano and double bass. I joined the Reuby because I believe it is a chance to create shared memories and foster a sense of belonging within the Reuben College community. I contributed to Reuby with some of my photographs and its digital publishing.

members.name: Carol Sun
members.bio: I'm a DPhil student studying on the Interdisciplinary Bioscience course, and I have always wanted to get involved in a student led magazine of some sort. I've contributed to the Reuby via an article on the art society I created, as well as some artistic direction. I've enjoyed sharing the work of others to a wider audience, and hope that this inspires people out there to get creative!
